Messages.Author: Boon Sian Chang
Messages.Body: Suppose WWEF is played, combat ensues, and the minion who played WWEF plays the superior form of Majesty, which allows him to untap. Is this allowed? Or does WWEF take precedence?

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <6chu5v$g...@ds2.acs.ucalgary.ca>, Boon Sian Chang
<bsc...@acs3.acs.ucalgary.ca> writes

>Suppose WWEF is played, combat ensues, and the minion who played WWEF plays the
>superior form of Majesty, which allows him to untap. Is this allowed? Or does
>WWEF take precedence?
>

Wake says nothing about remaining tapped. all it does is let you play
reaction cards and block as though untapped (which when you untap from
Majesty you can do anyway). It does not tap you as part of its effect.

Thus there is no conflict here. The vampire ends combat and, assuming
it burns the blood, it untaps.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
In article <6chu5v$g...@ds2.acs.ucalgary.ca>,

bsc...@acs3.acs.ucalgary.ca (Boon Sian Chang) wrote:
>
> Suppose WWEF is played, combat ensues, and the minion who played WWEF plays
the superior form of Majesty, which allows him to untap. Is this allowed? Or
does WWEF take precedence?

This is allowed.

The wakey's effect is not in conflict with Majesty's effect.
Wakey allows the vampire to play reaction cards and/or block
as if untapped.
Majesty is a combat card that allows the vampire to pay a
blood to untap (at superior).
